english.title: Fail to comply with regulations re travel departure from / arrival in UK under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a relevant offender within the terms of section 44 of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008, failed without reasonable excuse to notify the police of your

(A)_[departure from the United Kingdom before you left on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE OF DEPARTURE..)]_
(B)_[return to the United Kingdom on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE OR RETURN..)]_

in accordance with **(..SPECIFY THE REGULATIONS..), made under section 52(1) of the Act

english.notes:
(i) Section 52(2) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provides that notification of departure must disclose:-
(a) the date on which the person intends to leave the United Kingdom;
(b) the country (or, if there is more than one, the first country) to which the person will travel;
(c) the person's point of arrival (determined in accordance with the regulations) in that country;
(d) any other information required by the regulations.
(ii) Section 52(3) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provides that notification of return must disclose such information as is required by the regulations about the person's return to the United Kingdom.
(iii) Schedule 4 to the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 makes provision for the application of notification requirements to apply to persons who have been dealt with outside the United Kingdom in respect of a corresponding foreign offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 54(2) and (2A) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
